docs.title: ShutterBug Renderer
docs.text:
Take a photograph, stream a camera to a map, or compose a scene with your own lighting. Start with Renderer.forPlugin(this); the same API keeps manual scenes, assets, attachments and low-level rendering available when you need them.

These developer guides use ke.ric:renderer-api:2.3.0-preview.3, the free Apache-2.0 SDK with the new fluent API and creative controls. Use it with ShutterBug Renderer 1.1.0 and its matching embedded native library on macOS ARM64, Linux x86-64 or Windows x86-64. The published preview.3 SDK and its source/JavaDoc archives remain unchanged. Installing this SDK alone does not upgrade an older provider. The stable 2.2 SDK, historical previews and JitPack v1.0.2 remain available unchanged. See setup and IDE documentation and compatibility before choosing a build.

docs.title: A live camera in four lines
docs.text:
Create one Renderer with Renderer.forPlugin(this) in onEnable(). Then start a feed on the server thread, using an entity as camera and a player as viewer:

        RenderStream feed = renderer.stream(camera)
            .fov(75)
            .toPlayer(viewer)
            .start();

The viewer needs a free inventory slot for the live map. Keep feed and call feed.stop() when the monitor ends. To apply that viewer's visibility rules, also chain .visibleTo(viewer).

docs.title: Your first photo and live feed
docs.text:
This complete class adds a saved photograph and plugin cleanup:

package docs.examples;

import ke.ric.renderer.api.Renderer;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.RenderStream;
import org.bukkit.entity.Entity;
import org.bukkit.entity.Player;
import org.bukkit.plugin.java.JavaPlugin;

/** Call these methods from your plugin's commands or events on the server thread. */
public final class FluentExample extends JavaPlugin {
    private Renderer renderer;

    @Override public void onEnable() { renderer = Renderer.forPlugin(this); }

    public void photograph(Player player) {
        renderer.snapshot(player).fov(75).captureMap(item -> {
            // Callbacks run on the server thread. This example drops inventory overflow.
            if (player.isOnline()) player.getInventory().addItem(item).values().forEach(
                    extra -> player.getWorld().dropItemNaturally(player.getLocation(), extra));
        }, failure -> getLogger().warning("Photo failed: " + failure.getMessage()));
    }

    public RenderStream monitor(Entity camera, Player viewer) {
        RenderStream feed = renderer.stream(camera)
            .fov(75)
            .toPlayer(viewer)
            .start();
        return feed;
    }

    @Override public void onDisable() { if (renderer != null) renderer.close(); }
}

A photo is durably saved before the callback receives its map item. A stream reuses temporary map output and cleans up when stopped or when your plugin disables. Call stop() on the returned stream when that particular monitor ends. Raw capture() returns an image frame without allocating maps. Your plugin decides permissions, cooldowns and delivery; a production photo workflow should retain delivery for a player who disconnects while capture is running.

Defaults are CLASSIC, 128×128 pixels, a 70-degree vertical field of view and a 16-block radius. Builders are immutable: keep the value returned by each setting. Living entity cameras use eye position and exclude themselves. Callback overloads run on the server thread; ordinary futures retain ordinary Java threading rules.

Continue with capture and saved photos, live feeds, creative controls, or the small X-ray example. The API reference links every public type and the JavaDoc that also powers IDE hover descriptions.

docs.title: For server owners
docs.text: Begin with installation and activation. The commercial provider is installed separately and owns the renderer runtime. The free SDK does not contain or unlock it. The SDK compiles on Java 21; the documented Paper 26.2 / Minecraft 26.2 server requires Java 25. Use the platform archive for Renderer 1.1.0; see compatibility for the supported server runtime.

docs.title: Build free or paid add-ons
docs.text:
Both are welcome. You may sell plugins that depend on ShutterBug Renderer. Tell buyers that the provider is required and purchased separately: the server owner needs a valid provider license within its seat limits, not every player or a separate purchase per add-on on the same server. Do not redistribute the commercial provider, native binaries or activation credentials.

Examples 1.3.0 provides Postcards, Redstone Camera, Painter's Easel and Admin POV Monitor using the preview.3 SDK and Renderer 1.1.0. Start with the sample walkthrough.

The historical four-example release contains Postcards, Redstone Camera, Painter's Easel and Admin POV Monitor. That historical release uses SDK v1.0.2; its source is not evidence that an older provider supports the new fluent API. This guide's compiled examples use the current preview. Albums, collections, posing, item delivery and other gameplay belong to the consuming plugin.

docs.title: Assets
docs.text:
Register immutable ZIP bytes with the client before submission. Use the returned content hash in each job that needs the pack, retain the AssetHandle until all referencing tasks finish, and close it when the consumer no longer needs the registration. Handles and hashes are scoped to the owning client/provider generation; after reload, register the bytes again.

Treat MALFORMED_ASSET as a content error and MISSING_ASSET as a lifecycle/ownership error. On MISSING_ASSET, do not retry an inactive hash: re-register retained validated bytes with the current client, retain the replacement handle, recapture, rebuild the job with the replacement hash, and resubmit at most once. The returned recovery owner keeps that handle alive while the replacement task runs and closes it automatically when the task succeeds, fails, or is cancelled. Validate archive size and provenance before registration, never pass untrusted unbounded archives, and do not assume a file name is a content identity.

package docs.examples;

import ke.ric.renderer.api.AssetHandle;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.AssetPack;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.RenderJob;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.RenderSettings;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.RenderTask;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.RendererClient;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.Scene;

import java.util.List;

public final class AssetExample {
    public record AssetSubmission(AssetHandle asset, RenderTask task) implements AutoCloseable {
        @Override
        public void close() {
            asset.close();
        }
    }

    public static AssetSubmission submit(RendererClient client, Scene scene, byte[] zip) {
        AssetHandle asset = client.registerAsset(new AssetPack("consumer-pack.zip", zip));
        try {
            RenderSettings settings = RenderSettings.classic(scene.width(), scene.height());
            RenderTask task = client.submit(new RenderJob(1, scene, settings, List.of(asset.contentHash())));
            return new AssetSubmission(asset, task);
        } catch (RuntimeException failure) {
            asset.close();
            throw failure;
        }
    }
}

The returned AssetSubmission owns the registration. Keep it while the task is in flight, then close it after completion or cancellation has reached a terminal state.

Manual scenes carry engine-neutral evidence and may select registered assets, but they do not let consumers import provider-private meshes, native handles, or implementation classes. See manual scenes for completeness rules.

docs.title: Frames and provenance
docs.text:
RenderedFrame.image() / toBufferedImage() returns a new image of the final output. savePng(...) and toMapItem(...) convert asynchronously. For one pass, result() exposes native pixels, attachments, visibility and timings. getVisiblePlayers() and getVisibleEntities() return immutable identity records with UUIDs and visible-pixel counts; display names are not identities. Older results without native identity evidence report UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY, rather than inventing an empty list.

For layered recipes, inspect each RenderPassResult through passes(). The final composition has no single native depth/object/visibility buffer, so ambiguous aggregate evidence access is rejected. Conversion uses the final composed image.

provenance() separates captured facts from rendering overrides: source world, camera, capture interval, time/weather and camera biome. effectiveCamera() gives the actual rendering camera, including roll. These are optional where older/manual evidence cannot supply them. Source facts survive reframing and environment overrides. See creative controls and feed freshness.

docs.title: Native attachments
docs.text:
RGBA8 color is always present. Request optional DEPTH, NORMAL, MATERIAL_ID, or OBJECT_ID only when supportedAttachments() advertises it. An unrequested accessor returns null; result arrays and buffers are caller-owned defensive copies.

RenderTimings contains measured nanosecond phases. UNAVAILABLE means a phase did not occur inside the provider measurement boundary; zero is a real measurement. Use timings for diagnostics and comparison, not billing or guaranteed performance. VisibilityStatistics provides immutable semantic counts and pixel coverage for the completed frame; it is evidence from that render, not a world query.

package docs.examples;

import ke.ric.renderer.api.Attachment;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.RenderResult;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.RenderTimings;

public final class ResultInspectionExample {
    public static String summary(RenderResult result) {
        float[] depth = result.depth();
        String depthState = depth == null ? Attachment.DEPTH + " not requested" : depth.length + " depth pixels";
        RenderTimings timings = result.timings();
        return depthState + ", total=" + timings.totalNanos()
                + "ns, visible entities=" + result.visibility().entities();
    }
}

docs.title: Capture images and saved photos
docs.text:
Start with the compiled quickstart. renderer.snapshot(player).capture() returns a future of RenderedFrame; captureMap() returns a future of a durably saved map item. Their success/error callback overloads run on the server thread. Raw captures allocate no Minecraft maps.

Defaults are CLASSIC, 128×128 pixels, 70 degrees vertical FOV and a 16-block radius. Living entities use their eye pose at capture time and exclude themselves; nonliving entities use their location. A location source is copied when the builder is created. Set .resolution(width, height), .profile(...), .fov(...), .roll(...), .radius(...) or .settings(...) as needed. Builders are immutable.

Required chunks must already be loaded. Snapshots default to at most two chunks per tick. .chunksPerTick(...) adjusts the capture budget; it does not authorize loading cold chunks. Cancelling the returned future propagates to active capture/render/conversion work. Do not block the server thread with join() or get().

docs.title: Privacy and exclusions
docs.text:
.excluding(entities) accepts a collection of entities, including a list or set. Use .excludingIds(ids) for UUID collections. Inputs are copied, entity identities are sampled on the server thread, and exclusions apply before visual capture. .visibleTo(viewer) adds that viewer's Bukkit visibility rules. Output recipients alone do not define privacy.

Live capture also omits Spectator players and players with a true Bukkit vanished metadata value. If several plugins provide the flag, any true value wins. Ordinary invisibility effects or having vanish permissions are not equivalent to active vanish. Packet-only visibility cannot be inferred reliably without integration.

Visibility is frozen into a snapshot. Changing game mode or vanishing later cannot recall pixels in previously distributed photos. Live streams recheck viewer visibility during reuse and before publication. Filters and layered recipes can only select permitted captured evidence.

docs.title: Durable map output
docs.text:
captureMap() captures, converts and saves before publishing an item. frame.toMapItem() does the same output step for an existing frame. By default, one photo fits a 128×128 map with black aspect-preserving letterboxing. MapOutputOptions selects palette dithering. Conversion and atomic photo-record writes run off-thread; map attachment/allocation happens on the server thread.

The provider owns the original palette and stable photo identity, creator and creation time. Photo items are tagged so an administrator can identify and repair them. Normal restart restoration checks the world, map ID, flags and persisted random marker before attaching pixels. Unavailable worlds, missing bindings and mismatched identities preserve the photo data for recovery. A raw capture, PNG save or live stream does not enter this store.

A successful save does not guarantee inventory delivery: the consuming plugin owns offline players, full inventories, item metadata and mailboxes. Cancellation cannot undo a map allocation or atomic file replacement that has already completed. Photo storage and vanilla map saves are separate stores.

Back up provider photo storage, world map data/counter, inventories and consumer data together. See operator recovery before repairing a backup mismatch.

docs.title: Low-level capture remains available
docs.text:
Use renderer.client() or renderer.session() when composing exact entities, managing assets or submitting manual scenes. The existing constructors and capture methods remain available. This compiled fixture demonstrates the direct capture path:

package docs.examples;

import ke.ric.renderer.api.CaptureRequest;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.RenderJob;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.RenderResult;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.RenderSettings;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.RendererClient;
import org.bukkit.Location;

import java.util.Set;
import java.util.UUID;
import java.util.concurrent.CompletionStage;

public final class CaptureExample {
    public static CompletionStage<RenderResult> render(RendererClient client, Location camera) {
        RenderSettings settings = RenderSettings.classic(128, 128)
                .withProfile(RenderSettings.Profile.NORMAL);
        return client.capture(new CaptureRequest(camera, 32.0, settings, 4))
                .thenCompose(scene -> client.submit(new RenderJob(1, scene, settings)).completion());
    }

    public static CompletionStage<RenderResult> renderWithoutTarget(
            RendererClient client, Location camera, UUID target) {
        RenderSettings settings = RenderSettings.classic(128, 128);
        CaptureRequest capture = new CaptureRequest(camera, 16.0, settings, 2, Set.of(target));
        return client.capture(capture)
                .thenCompose(scene -> client.submit(new RenderJob(1, scene, settings)).completion());
    }
}

The original four-argument CaptureRequest constructor still uses an empty exclusion set. The five-argument constructor defensively copies excluded UUIDs. The FOV-aware capture overload rejects unsupported values on older providers instead of pretending they were applied. Do not reuse scenes or assets across provider generations.

docs.title: Maps inside photographs
docs.text:
Empty visible item frames use the installed Minecraft/resource-pack frame model: wooden border, inset backing, normal/glow textures, and all six mounting directions. Invisible empty frames stay absent. This does not add rendering of arbitrary items placed inside frames. Filled-map pixels, rotation and photographic feedback are unchanged.

Filled maps in ordinary or glow item frames use their last available map pixels as frozen scene textures. This includes the POV example's handheld map and desk screen: /pov ExactOnlinePlayerName and /pov demo use the same shareable, photographable screen. There is no private-screen mode or privacy-based gray replacement. Admin permissions still control who can start or change a feed; copied maps and other viewers can see its image.

Capturing a screen does not start another render. Looking into your own POV monitor therefore produces feedback across successive completed frames, not recursive work inside a single capture.

For third-party contextual maps (different pixels per viewer), the provider copies one existing complete cached view, using the same viewer for all contextual layers. It prefers an existing shared/null context; otherwise it deterministically selects the lowest player UUID with complete cached layers. This is not guaranteed to match the photographer's particular UI. Renderer callbacks and cursors are not captured.

A map whose custom renderer has not drawn yet, whose cached layers are incomplete, or whose server layout is unsupported still has no usable image and gets the normal unavailable-image placeholder. Let the map display normally first. This technical missing-data fallback does not censor available pixels.

docs.title: Renderer 1.1.0 and the fluent SDK
docs.text:
Pair ShutterBug Renderer 1.1.0 with ke.ric:renderer-api:2.3.0-preview.3 for fluent snapshots, live feeds, persistent photos, reuse and creative controls. Each commercial platform JAR embeds its matching native library. Updating a compile-time dependency alone does not upgrade an installed provider.

Platform key Renderer 1.1.0 status Runtime macos-aarch64 Supported macOS ARM64 linux-x86_64 Supported Linux x86-64 windows-x86_64 Supported Windows x86-64

Compile the SDK consumer on Java 21 or newer. The documented server runtime is Paper 26.2 build 129 / Minecraft 26.2 on Java 25. Support is for the packaged operating system/architecture pairs; other Paper revisions, server implementations, CPU architectures and operating systems are unverified. Windows support is based on the packaged provider/sample server checks; it does not claim Windows execution of the creative consumer or four-example probe. Server acceptance does not establish game-client visuals or a performance guarantee. Genuine personalized buyer activation remains pending separate verification.

The preview.3 coordinate, binary, sources, JavaDoc archive and versioned reference remain immutable. The stable Maven SDK 2.2, preview.1, preview.2 and historical JitPack SDK v1.0.2 also remain unchanged. Binary compatibility preserves existing consumers; it does not make a new method or native lighting contract available in an old provider. Unsupported controls fail explicitly. Consumers should check runtime capabilities.

docs.title: Historical Renderer 1.0.0
docs.text:
Renderer 1.0.0 used com.github.kernel-person:shutterbug-renderer-api:v1.0.2 and preserved the v1 public Java API and binary baseline. Its first delivery covered macOS ARM64 and Linux x86-64. A later three-platform delivery passed Windows acceptance on 18 October 2026, so Windows is no longer a coming-soon platform for that accepted delivery.

That Windows server run used Windows Server 2025 10.0 amd64, Paper 26.2 build 129 / Minecraft 26.2 and Eclipse Adoptium Temurin Java 25.0.4.1+1. The exact packaged Java/native pair passed the canary, initial activation, cached restart and clean shutdown. No Windows game client was launched. Same-release macOS checks ran natively on ARM64; Linux checks used Docker linux/amd64 emulation on the Mac, not a native Linux host. These historical results do not establish acceptance of a different artifact or genuine personalized buyer activation.

The frozen adapter identifier paper-26.2-minecraft-1.21.10 retains its historical compile-target name for compatibility; it is not an instruction to run Paper 26.2 on Java 21. Upgrading the commercial provider does not grant consumers permission to compile against private implementation packages.

docs.title: Convenient frame output
docs.text:
Use frame.image() for a newly allocated BufferedImage, frame.savePng(path) for asynchronous PNG encoding and atomic file replacement, or frame.toMapItem() for a provider-owned durable photo. captureMap() combines capture and map saving. The PNG parent directory must exist; unsupported atomic replacement or filesystem errors fail the future.

Saved-map delivery waits for persistence. One map is fitted with black aspect-preserving letterboxing; MapOutputOptions selects palette dithering. Raw capture and PNG output allocate no maps. See saved photos for backup and ownership semantics.

docs.title: Direct conversion and multi-map output
docs.text:
The existing conversion utilities remain available for custom filters, palettes and multi-map grouping. A consumer-owned MapSink receives an immutable MapFrame containing fitted palette bytes and the original frame evidence. The consuming plugin owns filtered-image identity, tile grouping, item delivery and any archival format beyond explicit provider photo saving.

Run nontrivial conversion off the main thread. PNG encoding preserves the result, while map quantization returns one map-palette byte per pixel. Map tiles require both dimensions to be multiples of 128. Store or transmit the returned copies under your plugin's own bounds and retention policy.

package docs.examples;

import ke.ric.renderer.api.MapDither;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.MinecraftMapConverter;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.PngConverter;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.RenderResult;

public final class ConversionExample {
    public static byte[] png(RenderResult frame) { return PngConverter.encode(frame); }
    public static byte[] map(RenderResult frame) { return MinecraftMapConverter.quantize(frame, MapDither.NONE); }
}

docs.title: Camera controls, layers and lighting
docs.text:
The same immutable controls work on snapshots and streams. These examples use only the public SDK and Bukkit types; each method returns a request you can finish with capture() or captureMap().

package docs.examples;

import ke.ric.renderer.api.*;
import org.bukkit.entity.Player;

/** Reusable requests: choose capture(), captureMap(), or further fluent settings. */
public final class CreativeControlsExample {
    public static SnapshotBuilder photograph(Renderer renderer, Player camera) {
        return renderer.snapshot(camera).fov(75).roll(12)
                .appearance(RenderAppearance.defaults().exposure(1.2))
                .environment(RenderEnvironment.captured().timeOfDay(6000).weather(Weather.CLEAR));
    }

    public static SnapshotBuilder highlight(Renderer renderer, Player viewer) {
        return renderer.snapshot(viewer).visibleTo(viewer).recipe(RenderRecipe.layers(
                RenderLayer.scene(),
                RenderLayer.entities(EntitySelector.living()).color(LayerColor.tint(0x80ffb0))));
    }

    public static SnapshotBuilder xray(Renderer renderer, Player viewer) {
        return renderer.snapshot(viewer).visibleTo(viewer).recipe(RenderRecipe.layers(
                RenderLayer.scene().brightness(0.2),
                RenderLayer.entities(EntitySelector.living())
                        .occlusion(Occlusion.SELECTED_ONLY).color(LayerColor.solid(0x80ffb0))));
    }

    public static SnapshotBuilder studio(Renderer renderer, Player camera) {
        var flash = new SpotLight(LightSpace.CAMERA, 0xffe0c0,
                0, 0.2, 0, new LightDirection(0, 0, 1), 3, 16, 45, 90, true);
        return renderer.snapshot(camera).lighting(RenderLighting.studio().ambient(0.1).add(flash));
    }
}

docs.title: Camera, environment and exposure
docs.text:
A Location supplies position, yaw and pitch. Living entity sources sample eye position and exclude themselves. .fov(degrees) changes vertical field of view and must be finite, greater than zero and less than 180. .roll(degrees) rotates around the viewing direction; it defaults to zero and must be finite. Advanced SceneCamera uses radians for roll.

RenderEnvironment.captured() inherits source time and weather. .timeOfDay(6000) or .weather(Weather.CLEAR) overrides rendering without changing the server world. With no weather override, rain/snow state follows captured local evidence. .weather(Weather.RAIN) or .weather(Weather.SNOW) explicitly chooses rendered precipitation without editing captured biomes.

Exposure changes lighting and tone mapping inside the renderer. Layer brightness multiplies the resulting RGB values. FOV, exposure and brightness are separate controls. Colour treatment runs first, then brightness, then opacity. LayerColor.tint(0xRRGGBB) multiplies colour; solid(0xRRGGBB) replaces it; original() preserves rendered colour. These treatments leave alpha unchanged until composition.

docs.title: Selection, occlusion and privacy
docs.text:
SceneContent.all(), blocksOnly() and entitiesOnly() select geometry. EntitySelector selects captured entities by UUID, type, living classification or players, and composes with and, or and not. .excluding(entities) accepts an entity collection, including lists and sets. .excludingIds(ids) accepts a UUID collection. Collection inputs are copied.

Entity layers default to Occlusion.RESPECT_SCENE. Blocks and nonselected entities can hide a selected entity, making visible-only highlighting a natural default. Explicit SELECTED_ONLY enables through-wall output; selected entities still obscure each other. It changes camera visibility while retaining the surrounding geometry for lighting, reflections and shadows.

Request-level content removal is stronger: SceneContent.entitiesOnly() removes blocks from all rays, including geometric shadows. Hiding a wall from output with an entity layer is therefore different from deleting its captured evidence. Use .visibleTo(viewer) for per-viewer Bukkit visibility rules. Request exclusions and privacy remain authoritative: selection and X-ray cannot bring excluded evidence back.

docs.title: Independent layers
docs.text:
Use RenderRecipe.layers(...) to compose ordered passes from one capture. Each layer can override content, environment, appearance and lighting; unspecified values inherit the request. Layer content intersects request content. Every pass derives independently from the same original capture, so a night setting or studio light rig in one layer does not leak into the next.

The final image, PNG and map outputs contain the composition. Read frame.passes() for native results and visibility of each pass. A multi-pass image has no single unambiguous object/depth buffer: result() and combined visible-entity getters reject that ambiguity. For a single pass, getVisiblePlayers() and getVisibleEntities() return immutable captured identities with UUIDs and visible-pixel coverage.

Advanced SceneTransform(content, environment, appearance) inherits existing lighting and primary visibility. In its six-argument overload, null lighting inherits, as does a null occlusion/selector pair. Explicit RenderLighting.world(), Occlusion.RESPECT_SCENE and EntitySelector.all() reset those controls.

docs.title: Build a light rig
docs.text:
RenderLighting.world() inherits existing lighting and preserves its original rendering path when unchanged. studio() starts with zero inherited ambient, sunlight and block light. Set .ambient(factor), .sun(factor) and .block(factor) independently; block control affects captured block illumination and coloured emitters. Sun direction follows rendered time unless .sunDirection(x, y, z) overrides the normalized direction from the surface toward the sun.

PointLight has a position. SpotLight adds direction and full inner/outer cone angles in degrees, fading smoothly between them. Both use RGB colour, artistic intensity, range in blocks and optional hard shadows. LightSpace.WORLD uses absolute world coordinates. CAMERA means right/up/forward and follows camera position, yaw, pitch and roll, including during scene reuse. The studio example therefore creates a camera-mounted flash without a Bukkit entity or a world mutation.

Initial per-pass limits are 16 virtual lights, eight shadow-casting lights, 64 blocks maximum range, and intensity 0–64. Ambient, sun and block factors also accept 0–64. Range must be positive. Cone angles require an inner angle at least zero, less than the outer angle, with the outer at most 180 degrees. Query renderer.client().lightingCapabilities() for provider limits. Invalid/excess requests and unsupported providers fail explicitly before rendering; requested virtual lights and shadows work in every supported quality profile.

Lighting uses actual hit normals and artistic diffuse response, including transparent surfaces and supported reflections. Shadow rays respect alpha cutouts; nonzero blended surfaces block hard shadows. Soft shadows, coloured transmission, arbitrary shaders, editable fog/biomes and transparent-background matting are outside this preview.

docs.title: Progress and captured facts
docs.text:
.onProgress(...) delivers FrameProgress on the server thread at most once per tick. Stages are CAPTURE, RENDER, CONVERSION and SAVING; basisPoints() measures work within that stage, with 10,000 meaning complete. Render progress identifies the zero-based pass and pass count. There is no estimated overall percentage, and fast transitions may be coalesced. Cancellation and lifecycle loss suppress late callbacks. Keep handlers short; normal futures retain Java continuation semantics.

frame.provenance() contains captured world UUID/name/environment, source camera, wall-clock capture instant, monotonic capture interval, full/day time, local precipitation, thunder and camera biome. effectiveCamera() describes the actual rendering camera, including roll. Overrides and reframing preserve source facts. Optional provenance may be absent for older providers or manually constructed evidence.

Batched capture retains and deduplicates generated-structure evidence. It requires loaded chunks and never silently loads missing scenery. Image filters, multi-map grouping, inventory delivery, albums, collections, posing and other gameplay remain consumer responsibilities.

docs.title: Typed failures
docs.text:
Handle RendererException by code(), never exception text. A lifecycle race may replace later work with the failure that wins. Unwrap completion wrappers first, then map stable codes to bounded actions:

  • Retry later with backoff after QUEUE_FULL; never spin.
  • Load required chunks and recapture after MISSING_CHUNK; recapture after STALE_SCENE.
  • Reduce dimensions, attachments, workers, or registered asset pressure after MEMORY_LIMIT; use a realistic deadline after TIMEOUT.
  • Close local state, rediscover the service, create a new client, and recapture after CLIENT_CLOSED or PROVIDER_DISABLED.
  • Select only advertised profiles/attachments after UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY; treat UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM as an operator compatibility issue.
  • Fix request input after INVALID_REQUEST; fix and revalidate archive bytes after MALFORMED_ASSET.
  • After MISSING_ASSET, never resubmit the same inactive hash. If the owner still has the bounded, validated ZIP bytes, register them with the current client, retain the replacement AssetHandle, recapture a scene for the current provider generation, rebuild the job with the replacement hash, and resubmit at most once. Keep the returned recovery owner until the replacement task terminates; it closes the replacement handle automatically after success, failure, or cancellation. If that recovery fails again, stop and report the lifecycle/ownership fault.
  • Report repeatable NATIVE_FAILURE with sanitized diagnostics and exact artifact checksums.
  • Treat CANCELLED as terminal when cancellation was requested.
package docs.examples;

import ke.ric.renderer.api.RendererException;

import java.util.concurrent.CompletionException;
import java.util.concurrent.ExecutionException;

public final class FailureExample {
    public static String code(Throwable failure) {
        Throwable cause = failure;
        while ((cause instanceof CompletionException || cause instanceof ExecutionException)
                && cause.getCause() != null) cause = cause.getCause();
        return cause instanceof RendererException renderer ? renderer.code().name() : "UNEXPECTED";
    }
}

package docs.examples;

import ke.ric.renderer.api.AssetHandle;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.AssetPack;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.RenderFailureCode;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.RenderJob;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.RenderSettings;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.RenderTask;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.RendererException;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.RendererClient;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.Scene;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicBoolean;

public final class RecoveryExample {
    public enum Action {
        RETRY_LATER,
        RECAPTURE,
        REREGISTER_ASSET_RECAPTURE_RESUBMIT,
        REDUCE_REQUEST,
        REDISCOVER_PROVIDER,
        REPORT
    }

    public static Action action(RendererException failure) {
        return action(failure.code());
    }

    public static Action action(RenderFailureCode code) {
        return switch (code) {
            case QUEUE_FULL -> Action.RETRY_LATER;
            case MISSING_CHUNK, STALE_SCENE -> Action.RECAPTURE;
            case MISSING_ASSET -> Action.REREGISTER_ASSET_RECAPTURE_RESUBMIT;
            case MEMORY_LIMIT, TIMEOUT -> Action.REDUCE_REQUEST;
            case CLIENT_CLOSED, PROVIDER_DISABLED -> Action.REDISCOVER_PROVIDER;
            default -> Action.REPORT;
        };
    }

    public static boolean mayRetryMissingAsset(RenderFailureCode code, int priorAssetRetries) {
        if (priorAssetRetries < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("negative retry count");
        return code == RenderFailureCode.MISSING_ASSET && priorAssetRetries == 0;
    }

    @FunctionalInterface
    public interface ReplacementSceneFactory {
        Scene rebuild(String replacementAssetHash);
    }

    public static AssetRecovery recoverMissingAssetOnce(RendererClient client, byte[] validatedZip,
                                                         ReplacementSceneFactory scenes,
                                                         RenderSettings settings,
                                                         int priorAssetRetries) {
        if (!mayRetryMissingAsset(RenderFailureCode.MISSING_ASSET, priorAssetRetries)) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("missing-asset recovery is limited to one attempt");
        }
        AssetHandle replacement = client.registerAsset(
                new AssetPack("consumer-pack.zip", validatedZip));
        try {
            String replacementHash = replacement.contentHash();
            Scene replacementScene = scenes.rebuild(replacementHash);
            RenderTask replacementTask = client.submit(new RenderJob(
                    1, replacementScene, settings, List.of(replacementHash)));
            AssetRecovery recovery = new AssetRecovery(replacement, replacementTask);
            replacementTask.completion().whenComplete((result, failure) -> recovery.close());
            return recovery;
        } catch (RuntimeException failure) {
            replacement.close();
            throw failure;
        }
    }

    public static final class AssetRecovery implements AutoCloseable {
        private final AssetHandle replacement;
        private final RenderTask task;
        private final AtomicBoolean closed = new AtomicBoolean();

        private AssetRecovery(AssetHandle replacement, RenderTask task) {
            this.replacement = replacement;
            this.task = task;
        }

        public AssetHandle replacement() {
            return replacement;
        }

        public RenderTask task() {
            return task;
        }

        @Override
        public void close() {
            if (closed.compareAndSet(false, true)) replacement.close();
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Snapshot and stream progress
docs.text:
.onProgress(...) receives measured FrameProgress for capture, each render pass, conversion and saving. Callbacks run on the server thread at most once per tick. basisPoints() ranges from zero to 10,000 within the current stage, and rendering identifies its pass index/count. A new stage or pass can restart at zero; this is not an estimated total duration or overall percentage. Updates are coalesced, so callers must not depend on receiving every transition.

Cancel a snapshot's returned future to cancel its current stage. Stop a stream to end future frames and remove owned temporary output. Cancellation and lifecycle loss suppress late callbacks. A completed map allocation or atomic file write cannot be undone by cancelling a later step.

docs.title: Low-level jobs
docs.text:
submit performs bounded admission and returns a RenderTask; queue admission can fail synchronously with QUEUE_FULL. The provider defaults to one concurrent native render, queue capacity 16 and a 512 MiB aggregate native-memory budget. An operator can configure concurrency; consumers must still respect admission and memory failures. A job's effective memory ceiling is the lower of its requested limit and the provider limit. Admission reserves scene, selected assets, render, attachment and copy memory, and releases the reservation on every terminal path. Manual scene construction and asset registration are bounded too.

RenderSettings.timeout() begins at task creation and covers queueing, preparation, native work, diagnostics, and output copy. Poll progress() without blocking: phases are QUEUED, PREPARING, DECODING, RENDERING, POST_PROCESSING, DIAGNOSTICS, COPYING_OUTPUT, and terminal COMPLETE. Progress is monotonic actual work, not a wall-clock estimate; successful completion is COMPLETE/10_000.

cancel() returns true only when it wins a nonterminal transition; completion then fails with CANCELLED, while a terminal race returns false. status() is the coarse task state. Bound concurrent submissions in the consumer, back off after QUEUE_FULL, and retain a task only until its completion/cancellation handling finishes. See the complete sample plugin.

docs.title: Plugin-owned facade
docs.text:
For the new API, create one Renderer.forPlugin(this) in onEnable() and close it from onDisable(), on the server thread. The quickstart is a complete compiled example. The facade owns capture/render work, listeners, temporary streams and a bounded conversion worker. Owner disable also triggers cleanup automatically. Saved provider photos survive this cleanup.

Service discovery is lazy: when no provider is ready, a new operation fails with PROVIDER_DISABLED. Provider replacement invalidates existing work; later requests can discover the new provider. Do not carry captured scenes or assets across generations. Affected world unload also invalidates pending work. Use the facade's callback overloads for Bukkit delivery and keep callbacks short.

renderer.session() and renderer.client() retain the advanced API. If you manage a separate low-level client, you own its lifecycle as shown below.

docs.title: Direct clients and optional providers
docs.text:
For a hard dependency, direct API imports are safe: load RendererService, create one client for your plugin, retain it in the lifecycle owner, and call close() during disable. After a provider reload, discover a new service and client; do not retain old clients, assets, scenes, or tasks. See the complete sample plugin.

package docs.examples;

import ke.ric.renderer.api.RendererClient;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.RendererService;
import org.bukkit.Bukkit;
import org.bukkit.plugin.Plugin;

public final class LifecycleExample {
    public static RendererClient discover(Plugin owner) {
        RendererService service = Bukkit.getServicesManager().load(RendererService.class);
        return service == null ? null : service.createClient(owner);
    }
}

For softdepend, the Bukkit entry point must contain no API imports or symbolic API references, because the provided API can be absent before discovery. Use an API-free entry point that reflectively loads an isolated API runtime only after checking availability. Retry discovery when the asynchronously starting provider registers RendererService; do not busy-loop or enable twice.

package docs.examples;

import org.bukkit.plugin.java.JavaPlugin;

/** API-free entry point for a soft-dependent consumer. */
public final class OptionalProviderEntrypoint extends JavaPlugin {
    @Override public void onEnable() {
        try {
            Class.forName("ke.ric.renderer.api.RendererService", false, getClassLoader());
            Class.forName("docs.examples.OptionalRendererRuntime", true, getClassLoader())
                    .getMethod("enable", JavaPlugin.class).invoke(null, this);
        } catch (ReflectiveOperationException | LinkageError unavailable) {
            getLogger().warning("Renderer API/provider is unavailable; continuing without rendering");
        }
    }
    @Override public void onDisable() {
        try { Class.forName("docs.examples.OptionalRendererRuntime", false, getClassLoader())
                .getMethod("disable").invoke(null); }
        catch (ReflectiveOperationException | LinkageError ignored) { }
    }
}

package docs.examples;

import ke.ric.renderer.api.RendererClient;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.RendererService;
import org.bukkit.Bukkit;
import org.bukkit.event.EventHandler;
import org.bukkit.event.HandlerList;
import org.bukkit.event.Listener;
import org.bukkit.event.server.ServiceRegisterEvent;
import org.bukkit.plugin.java.JavaPlugin;

/** Isolated API-linked runtime loaded only after the API-free entry point checks availability. */
public final class OptionalRendererRuntime {
    private static JavaPlugin owner;
    private static Listener registrationListener;
    private static RendererClient client;

    public static synchronized void enable(JavaPlugin plugin) {
        if (owner != null) return;
        owner = java.util.Objects.requireNonNull(plugin, "plugin");
        registrationListener = new Listener() {
            @EventHandler
            public void onServiceRegister(ServiceRegisterEvent event) {
                if (event.getProvider().getService() == RendererService.class) attach();
            }
        };
        Bukkit.getPluginManager().registerEvents(registrationListener, plugin);
        attach();
    }

    private static synchronized void attach() {
        if (owner == null || client != null) return;
        RendererService service = Bukkit.getServicesManager().load(RendererService.class);
        if (service == null) return;
        client = service.createClient(owner);
    }

    public static void disable() {
        RendererClient closingClient;
        Listener closingListener;
        synchronized (OptionalRendererRuntime.class) {
            closingClient = client;
            closingListener = registrationListener;
            client = null;
            registrationListener = null;
            owner = null;
        }
        if (closingListener != null) HandlerList.unregisterAll(closingListener);
        if (closingClient != null) closingClient.close();
    }
}

docs.title: Live cameras and screens
docs.text: A feed starts with renderer.stream(camera) and ends with stop() or close() on its RenderStream. The quickstart contains a compiled handheld example. Snapshot and stream builders share FOV, roll, quality, radius, exclusions, content, environment, appearance, lighting and recipe controls.

docs.title: Choose a camera and output
docs.text:
An entity source follows its eye position if living, otherwise its location, and excludes that entity. A fixed Location is copied. A location supplier is evaluated on the server thread when useful work can begin: return null to end the feed; a thrown exception fails it. Keep suppliers fast and do not load chunks in them.

.toPlayer(viewer) places one owned temporary map in a free inventory slot. It never replaces an existing item and rejects a full inventory. The image fits one map with aspect-preserving letterboxing. Disconnect removes that output.

.toScreen(anchor, BlockFace.NORTH, 2, 2) creates a two-by-two map screen. The anchor is a Location of the upper-left backing block as viewed from the requested outward face. Columns extend right and rows down. NORTH, SOUTH, EAST and WEST are supported. The wall must be solid, loaded and unobstructed. Existing item frames are rejected; the renderer creates temporary frames and rolls back partial setup if placement fails. With no explicit resolution, each grid cell contributes 128×128 pixels. An explicit resolution is fitted to the output while retaining aspect ratio.

Combine output calls to display the same feed in several places. .onFrame(...) receives frames without allocating maps and may be combined with outputs. .toMapSink(...) updates a receiver your plugin already owns; receiver identity, permissions and persistence remain your responsibility. Existing receivers must follow the public MapSink contract.

docs.title: Smoothness and freshness
docs.text:
Streams target 20 FPS, with supported targets from 1 through 20. This is a scheduling target, not a throughput guarantee. Smooth mode can reframe world evidence for up to 500 ms, two blocks of camera movement and within the captured center chunk. Reframing updates camera pose, including camera-relative lights; it does not recapture moving entities or world geometry. .fresh() requests new world evidence every frame. .reuse(Duration, displacement) exposes explicit reuse bounds.

A fair coordinator shares a four-chunk-per-tick capture budget between convenience streams. Each stream keeps at most one render/conversion in flight. Temporary overload skips work instead of accumulating catch-up frames; obsolete frames cannot rewind a displayed feed. After one second without a usable frame, map output displays “No signal” until recovery.

Measure delivered FPS, camera age, world age and server performance separately. cameraCapturedNanos(), worldCapturedNanos() and publishedNanos() use the monotonic System.nanoTime() domain. World age starts at the first captured world read and survives reuse. Captured facts in provenance() remain unchanged by environment or camera overrides.

docs.title: Ownership, privacy and failure
docs.text:
Call .visibleTo(viewer) explicitly when a feed should respect that viewer's Bukkit visibility rules. Output recipients do not implicitly define privacy because a public screen may have many viewers. Visibility is rechecked during reuse and before publication; exclusions cannot be undone by an X-ray layer.

Source death/logout, a null location supplier, owner disable, provider replacement and affected world unload end or fail the relevant work. .onError(...) reports both permanent failures and recoverable skipped frames; normal temporary overload uses bounded retries. status(), lastError(), lastFrame() and completion() expose feed state. Callback consumers run on the server thread and should remain short.

Stopping removes only owned temporary items and frames. It preserves unrelated items and backing blocks. Losing the last output stops a feed unless a frame consumer remains. Live stream maps do not enter photo storage; saved photos use explicit captureMap() or toMapItem() instead.

docs.title: Manual scenes
docs.text:
Use manual scenes only for complete caller-supplied engine-neutral evidence. Declare output dimensions, camera, world identity and height, weather, required chunks, every required section state, blocks, entities, structures, and resolved visuals needed by the scene. The builder rejects incomplete evidence instead of guessing. Scene instances belong to the client/provider generation that created them and must be rebuilt after reload. See assets for pack ownership.

package docs.examples;

import ke.ric.renderer.api.ChunkSectionState;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.RendererClient;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.Scene;

public final class ManualSceneExample {
    public static Scene create(RendererClient client) {
        return client.newSceneBuilder().dimensions(64, 64)
                .camera(0.5, 2.0, 5.0, 0.0, 0.0, Math.toRadians(70.0))
                .world("minecraft:overworld", "manual", 6_000L, 0, 16)
                .weather(false, false).block(0, 0, 0, "minecraft:stone", 0, 15, "minecraft:plains")
                .requireChunk(0, 0).chunkSection(0, 0, 0, ChunkSectionState.PALETTED).build();
    }
}

docs.title: Operator installation and activation
docs.text:
Renderer 1.1.0 supplies the fluent/creative API used by the immutable 2.3.0-preview.3 SDK. Upgrade the installed provider and its matching platform JAR together with any dependent plugin changes; an SDK dependency alone does not upgrade Renderer 1.0.0. See compatibility.

ShutterBug Renderer 1.1.0 is a separately installed commercial provider by Kernel Person. Stop the server and copy only the personalized ShutterBugRenderer.jar from your MCModels download for the server platform into plugins/. The matching native .so, .dylib or .dll is embedded in that JAR, checksum-verified, and extracted automatically to the provider's managed cache. Do not install a separate native file. Start the server and read the provider startup result before enabling dependent plugins. The supported platforms are macOS ARM64, Linux x86-64 and Windows x86-64. Use the archive matching the server operating system and CPU architecture.

docs.title: Activate safely
docs.text:
Automatic activation is designed for a personalized MCModels download: when the Renderer-specific buyer flow is verified and enabled, leave plugins/ShutterBugRenderer/config.yml's license-key field blank and the JAR's purchase information supplies activation. That production buyer flow is currently pending separate verification; do not treat SDK publication or a generic download as evidence that automatic issuance is enabled. Start Paper on Java 25 with Paper 26.2 / Minecraft 26.2 and wait for the provider startup result. A non-personalized or incomplete JAR cannot activate merely because it was copied into plugins/.

If support supplies a separate manual activation value, start Paper once to generate plugins/ShutterBugRenderer/config.yml, stop the server, and set that value in license-key. An explicitly configured manual value takes precedence over the personalized-download information for fresh activation. Restrict the config and its backups so only the Paper server account can read them. Never print or copy activation values into logs, shell history, tickets, screenshots, startup arguments, or public issues. Restart after changing the value; do not hot-edit provider files while jobs are running.

Successful activation means the provider reports the expected product identity, the service becomes available, and capabilities report both native availability and production packaging. If any check fails, leave dependent plugins in optional/fallback mode and follow troubleshooting. Never weaken a check or copy a license between customers to make startup continue.

docs.title: Leases and seats
docs.text:
One purchase permits three active hardware installations. Each signed lease has a six-hour validity window; renewal normally happens while the provider is running, and expired evidence fails closed. A valid signed cached lease can support a restart during a short activation-service outage until it expires; the cache is time-limited and is not a permanent activation bypass.

A clean shutdown closes the provider and clears local runtime state, but it does not send a backend deactivation request and therefore must not be presented as immediately freeing a remote hardware seat. For a permanent host change or a stale seat, stop the old server, retain its sanitized logs, and follow the supported operator/admin process for a hardware-seat change or reset. There is no customer self-service endpoint documented by this provider.

Do not automate repeated activation attempts. Treat not entitled, seat limit, lease unavailable, clock/trust, and product mismatch as operator actions, not renderer retries. Support may ask for product version, platform key, provider startup code, sanitized capability output, and artifact checksums; never include the license value or full environment dumps.

docs.title: Disable or remove
docs.text: Stop submissions, disable dependent plugins, and perform a clean server shutdown before removing the provider. Keep the release archive and its checksums for rollback. Removing the provider does not remove the free API from developer builds, but hard-dependent plugins will no longer start.

docs.title: Saved photos in Renderer 1.1.0
docs.text:
Renderer 1.1.0 saves photo palettes and stable identities in plugins/ShutterBugRenderer/photos/. A successful captureMap() finishes persistence before returning the item. Streams use temporary maps and never enter this store. Normal startup indexes records asynchronously, restores valid map bindings on the server thread and waits for worlds that load later. Startup status distinguishes indexed photos from maps actually restored.

Administrators with shutterbugrenderer.admin can use:

Command Purpose /renderer status Check render/photo readiness, indexed and restored totals, storage issues and unavailable worlds. /renderer storage Inspect saved-map counts and actual disk usage grouped by creator plugin. /renderer repair Repair the tagged renderer photo in your main hand, retaining photo identity and item metadata.

Storage notices default to 10,000 saved maps or 256 MiB. Configure photos.warn-maps and photos.warn-bytes; zero disables that notice. They report at startup when already exceeded and when crossing a threshold. Notices neither delete photos nor prevent saving. photos.palette-cache-maps bounds the palette cache, defaults to 64, and accepts 1–4096.

Back up the world save, vanilla map data and global map counter, inventories/item metadata, provider photo storage and consumer-owned data together. A photo palette alone is not a matching vanilla map backup. Keep original records and backups while investigating corruption; one bad record does not discard the library.

If saving fails, check the reported storage path, free space and filesystem permissions, correct the problem and retry the photograph. An unhealthy photo store does not imply raw rendering is unavailable. If the source world is unavailable, load that world before restoration/repair can complete.

If map identity differs after restoring mismatched backups, the provider preserves the photo bytes and refuses to overwrite an unrelated map. Use a consistent backup, or hold a tagged photo and run /renderer repair to reuse a valid binding or allocate a safe replacement. Repair rechecks the held item before delivery. Missing or corrupt source records require recovery from backup.

If allocation reports a rolled-back global map counter, restore matching vanilla map data/counter and restart. The provider does not rewrite world files automatically or overwrite occupied IDs. Repair cannot bypass an unsafe allocator.

docs.title: Profiles and capabilities
docs.text:
The fluent API defaults to CLASSIC at 128×128. Set .profile(...) and .resolution(width, height) independently, or supply RenderSettings for attachments and advanced limits. Higher quality or larger images can reduce delivered feed rate; 20 FPS remains a scheduling target.

Explicit point/spot lights and requested shadows work in every supported profile. Captured world-emitter detail still follows the existing profile. Query renderer.client().lightingCapabilities() for creative-light limits as well as the general capabilities below. Older providers explicitly reject unavailable controls.

Check RendererCapabilities.supportedProfiles() before submission. The stable names are CLASSIC, CLASSIC_HQ, NORMAL, CINEMATIC, ULTRA, ULTRA_PLUS, and EXTREME. A consumer should select a supported fallback rather than assume every provider exposes every profile. nativeAvailable() reports current runtime availability; packagedForProduction() reports verified package identity, not license state or general development usability. Keep operator activation failures separate from API capability handling.

docs.title: Renderer 1.1.0
docs.text:
Renderer 1.1.0 pairs the commercial provider and embedded native library with the existing ke.ric:renderer-api:2.3.0-preview.3 SDK. It adds the fluent snapshot/stream API, persistent photos, scene reuse and creative controls described below. Platform archives are available for macOS ARM64, Linux x86-64 and Windows x86-64; the documented server runtime is Paper 26.2 / Minecraft 26.2 on Java 25. See compatibility and upgrade steps.

This provider release does not republish the SDK: preview.3 binary, source and JavaDoc archives, versioned reference pages, checksums and earlier releases remain unchanged. The preview suffix remains part of the immutable SDK coordinate. Personalized buyer activation remains a separate verification gate.

docs.title: Examples 1.3.0
docs.text: Examples 1.3.0 pairs Postcards, Redstone Camera, Painter's Easel and Admin POV Monitor with the public 2.3.0-preview.3 SDK and separately installed Renderer 1.1.0. The free examples include their source and plugin JARs; they do not include the commercial provider. See the sample walkthrough for controls and setup. Historical Examples 1.2.0 and its SDK v1.0.2 references remain unchanged.

docs.title: SDK 2.3.0-preview.3 — fluent and creative controls
docs.text:
This immutable SDK adds Renderer.forPlugin(...), immutable snapshot/stream builders, automatic saved-photo map output, temporary handheld/screens and advanced session/client access. It includes collection exclusions, content/environment/appearance controls, reusable layered recipes, roll, tint/solid colour, independent ambient/sun/block lighting, point/spot lights, stage progress and capture provenance.

Entity layers respect scene occlusion by default. Through-wall rendering is explicit with Occlusion.SELECTED_ONLY; request privacy/exclusions remain authoritative. Live feeds target 20 FPS and use bounded scene reuse by default, with .fresh() for a capture each frame. Actual delivery depends on resolution, scene, lighting and server load.

The SDK ships matching source and JavaDoc companions and parameter metadata for IDE help. Originally published for the matching development provider, it is now paired with Renderer 1.1.0. Stable Maven 2.2, earlier previews and JitPack tags remain unchanged.

The original public constructors and v1 binary baseline remain preserved. The entity-layer default is a change within the previously unpublished development API. See setup, creative controls and compatibility.

docs.title: SDK v1.0.2
docs.text:
This published release adds target-specific entity exclusions to CaptureRequest: callers can pass an immutable set of UUIDs to omit before visual capture. The original four-argument constructor remains available with an empty exclusion set. Existing v1 binaries remain compatible, and the frozen v1 baseline is unchanged. Source consumers using record deconstruction or record-component reflection must account for the fifth component; see upgrading. The immutable v1.0.2 tag and JitPack build are published and verified through fresh Maven and Gradle consumers; no previous tag is moved or rewritten. The public JitPack JAR also passes the API boundary and frozen binary compatibility checks. See the SDK release.

The guides describe photographable shared POV screens, best-effort 4 Hz default cadence with /pov demo 1 through /pov demo 20, six-direction camera mounting, and captured map pixels. Published Examples 1.2.0 use this SDK and reuse the byte-identical renderer-examples-resourcepack-1.1.0.zip. Free-source publication does not establish matching-provider Paper acceptance or genuine buyer activation. The later Renderer 1.0.0 delivery passed Windows server acceptance on 18 October 2026; this does not change the immutable SDK or example artifacts.

docs.title: SDK v1.0.1 (previous release)
docs.text: The free SDK distribution is already published at JitPack tag v1.0.1. Its public packages, signatures, and v1 binary baseline are unchanged. This documentation update adds personalized-download activation guidance and current example controls without changing or retagging the SDK. The existing guides also cover Maven and Gradle consumer builds, public-type Javadocs, compatibility, recovery, and deterministic documentation/export verification.

docs.title: Renderer 1.0.0
docs.text: Renderer 1.0.0 is the previous commercial release. The MCModels personalized download is designed to activate automatically; a configured manual value remains an override and signed cached leases support bounded restarts. One purchase allows three active hardware installations with six-hour leases. Its first delivery supported macOS ARM64 and Linux x86-64. The later three-platform delivery passed Windows x86-64 server acceptance on 18 October 2026, including initial activation, cached restart and clean shutdown on Windows Server 2025, Paper 26.2 build 129 and Java 25. Client visuals and genuine personalized buyer activation were not established by those server checks.

docs.title: Start with the new fluent examples
docs.text:
For a new integration, begin with the compiled photo/stream quickstart, small X-ray camera or creative lighting examples. They use ke.ric:renderer-api:2.3.0-preview.3 and ShutterBug Renderer 1.1.0 with its matching embedded native library. Most ordinary capture/render/conversion ownership now belongs to the facade.

Use Examples 1.3.0 with Renderer 1.1.0 and the public preview.3 SDK for Postcards, Redstone Camera, Painter's Easel and Admin POV Monitor. The provider is purchased and installed separately.

The lower-level v1.0.2 sample and Examples 1.2.0 references below are retained as historical release references. Their versioned source demonstrates explicit orchestration and consumer gameplay; it does not imply that an older provider supports new controls.

docs.title: Advanced low-level sample
docs.text:
The sibling sample-plugin is a buildable external consumer, not pseudocode. With Java 21, run mvn -B clean install, then mvn -B -f sample-plugin/pom.xml clean verify from the exported SDK repository.

Follow its lifecycle in order:

  1. The Bukkit entry point remains API-free so softdepend can start when the SDK/provider is absent.
  2. The isolated runtime attaches immediately when the service exists and listens for asynchronous service registration without double activation.
  3. It creates one client owned by the plugin, reads capabilities, and chooses only advertised profiles/attachments.
  4. The sample explicitly prepares cold regions asynchronously, then passes loaded evidence to bounded capture and rejects stale lifecycle state. The renderer API itself never silently loads missing chunks.
  5. It submits a bounded job, polls monotonic progress, observes cancellation/timeout, and handles typed failures.
  6. It inspects immutable results, timings, and visibility, then performs PNG/map conversion off-thread.
  7. Disable closes polling, tasks, assets, and the client. A provider reload requires discovery, a new client, and fresh capture.

Before adapting the sample, decide whether rendering is optional, bound your queues and retained output, preserve the safe operator boundary, and keep provider-private packages out of your build.

docs.title: Four playable Java examples
docs.text:
For smaller starting points, use shutterbug-renderer-examples. Each module is independently installable, depends on the public SDK with provided scope, and requires the separately installed commercial provider. None handles activation credentials or includes native binaries.

Build the examples repository with mvn clean verify on JDK21 or newer. Copy any module's target/Renderer*.jar into your server's plugins folder and restart. The tested server runtime is Java25, Paper26.2 and Minecraft26.2; see compatibility.

  1. Postcards: run /postcard with an empty inventory slot. Expect a persistent map of your view. Read its short command handler, then its lifecycle and map helpers.
  2. Redstone Camera: as an operator, run /rendercamera and place the dispenser. Its lens faces toward the placer in one of six orthogonal directions: north, south, east, west, up or down. Aim through placement; free-angle yaw/pitch is not supported. An accepted redstone-triggered capture emits a brief white flash outside the lens (enable client particles), then the finished map appears in the inventory. The flash means capture started, not that it succeeded; wait for the high success tone before collecting the photo. Sustained power does not repeatedly photograph; busy, unavailable and full-inventory requests do not flash. Break and place a new camera to change its aim.

  3. Painter's Easel: as an operator, run /easel, place the easel, and brush-right-click its canvas for one fixed reference capture. Put cyan, magenta, or yellow dye in your offhand, then hold right-click and drag the brush across the map; punching also paints. The roughly 24-pixel round brush joins nearby input samples into continuous strokes. Sneak-right-click collects the painting. Capture happens once, not on each stroke.

  4. Admin POV Monitor: as an operator with rendererexamples.pov, run /pov ExactOnlinePlayerName and hold the supplied map in either hand. /pov monitor supplies a desk monitor; place it with two blocks of height and space in front. Watch your own loaded screen within 16 blocks with line of sight to keep the feed active. /pov stop blanks the feed. Anyone can see or photograph the receiver or monitor, including copied maps; there is no private mode. Command access and monitor placement/removal remain owner-controlled. The view is periodic rendering of the target's eye position and yaw/pitch, not screen sharing: no HUD, chat, inventory, client shaders or audio.

POV uses 128 by 128 CLASSIC frames, a 16-block radius, two capture chunks per tick and one native worker. At most two target feeds and one capture/render pipeline run globally. The default target is four updates per second per feed. /pov demo 4 selects your self-view and sets the shared server-run target rate; integers 1–20 are accepted, and a restart restores 4. Plain /pov demo keeps the current rate. This is best-effort, not a latency guarantee: slow work skips intervals, failures back off and delayed frames show STALE. Raising the target never adds parallel jobs or queued frames. No frames are archived. Permission loss, target disappearance, teleport/world changes and provider reload invalidate applicable work. No chunks are generated or synchronously loaded.

For optional native visuals, host the examples' renderer-examples-resourcepack-1.1.0.zip over player-reachable HTTPS and configure the server to offer it. Examples 1.2.0 include this byte-identical pack unchanged. Compute the SHA-1 from the exact file served (shasum -a 1 renderer-examples-resourcepack-1.1.0.zip on macOS or sha1sum on Linux); marketplace repacking may change ZIP bytes. Do not reuse the historical 1.0.0 pack hash. Set native-models: true in both camera and POV plugin configurations. In plugins/RendererPaintersEasel/config.yml, set model-item: village_trades:painters_easel and brush-model-item: village_trades:paintbrush, then restart. The pack adds camera optics, a thick opaque linen backing behind the live easel map, the original brush and a desk monitor around a real map. No Nexo or extra plugin is needed, and vanilla items are not globally replaced. Players must accept the pack. It targets Minecraft 26.2; the latest visual acceptance status is recorded separately in the examples repository.

docs.title: Record a solo demonstration
docs.text:
Use /pov YourExactPlayerName or /pov demo to target yourself; both use the same photographable receiver. Hold the map in your offhand, slowly turn between scenes and pause for snapshots. Face your desk monitor for several updates to capture the previous completed frame inside the next one. Finish with /pov stop. Label the clip solo self-view demo, not another player's POV or real-time screen sharing. For another player's view, use a second legitimate account/client or an invited tester; keep server authentication enabled. A solo clip does not establish multi-user command authorization or measured rendering latency.

The recording guide includes shot lists for painting, camera flash/photo pickup and POV. Final examples acceptance and the separate marketplace buyer-activation gate must pass before treating the product as sales-ready.

The examples repository README contains the full controls, permissions, persistence, and adaptation notes. Its acceptance document separates human client playtesting from automated tests and from final packaged-artifact verification. The examples have no economy dependency.

You may adapt the Apache-2.0 example source for free or paid add-ons, retaining required notices. Tell buyers “Requires ShutterBug Renderer, purchased separately.” Distribute your add-on only, not the commercial provider.

docs.title: Maven, Gradle and IDE setup
docs.text:
Use ke.ric:renderer-api:2.3.0-preview.3 for the fluent snapshot/stream API, scene recipes and creative lighting. Pair it with ShutterBug Renderer 1.1.0, whose platform JAR includes the matching native library. Stable ke.ric:renderer-api:2.2, earlier preview versions and the historical JitPack v1.0.2 release remain unchanged and do not supply these additions. The preview.3 coordinate and all published SDK, source and JavaDoc bytes remain unchanged. Renderer 1.0.0 does not acquire these additions from a compile-time dependency update.

Compile your plugin with Java 21 or newer. The documented Paper 26.2 / Minecraft 26.2 server requires Java 25. Use the API as a provided or compileOnly dependency; do not shade, relocate or bundle it. The separately installed ShutterBugRenderer supplies runtime API classes.
