The Bukkit dependency below is a Java 21 compile-time surface for these examples, not a promise that the provider runs against every Spigot/Paper version. Match the provider's exact Paper adapter when running it. Both consumer builds compile this fluent API probe:

package docs.examples;

import ke.ric.renderer.api.Renderer;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.RenderRecipe;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.RenderLayer;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.EntitySelector;
import ke.ric.renderer.api.SnapshotBuilder;
import org.bukkit.entity.Player;

/** Both dependency examples compile the fluent API, not just an older capability method. */
public final class ConsumerExample {
    public static SnapshotBuilder photo(Renderer renderer, Player player) {
        return renderer.snapshot(player).fov(75).roll(5).visibleTo(player)
                .recipe(RenderRecipe.layers(RenderLayer.scene(),
                        RenderLayer.entities(EntitySelector.living())));
    }
}

Use depend: [ShutterBugRenderer] when rendering is mandatory. Use softdepend: [ShutterBugRenderer] only when your plugin remains useful without rendering; follow the API-free entry-point pattern in lifecycle.

docs.title: Descriptions and parameter names in your editor
docs.text:
The SDK has matching sources and JavaDoc JARs, plus Java parameter-name metadata. IDEs use these for method descriptions, units, defaults, argument help and source navigation. The same reference is available in your browser.

In IntelliJ IDEA, reload the Maven/Gradle project and use the dependency's Download Sources and Download Documentation actions if automatic downloading is disabled. Open Quick Documentation on a method for its description and parameter details.

In VS Code, reload the Maven project after changing versions. Enable Java › Inlay Hints › Parameter Names: Enabled, choosing literals or all. Inlay hints are editor decorations, not Java syntax. If stale missing-source results remain cached, run Java: Clean Java Language Server Workspace, then reload. Hover a method to see its documentation.

If autocomplete still lacks Renderer, SnapshotBuilder or RenderLighting, check the resolved dependency version and remove duplicate older SDK dependencies. A provider update cannot change the classes your IDE compiles against, and a newer compile dependency cannot add runtime support to an older provider.

docs.title: Keep advanced access
docs.text: renderer.session() exposes lifecycle-aware capture/composition helpers, and renderer.client() exposes scene builders, assets, attachments, manual submission and provider capabilities. Start with the quickstart; use the advanced pages when your integration needs them.

docs.title: Threading and cancellation
docs.text:
Create/close the plugin-owned Renderer, start streams, and perform Bukkit operations on the server thread. Capture reads loaded world evidence in bounded server-thread batches. Entity pose, location suppliers and environment suppliers are sampled there. Native rendering, substantial conversion and provider photo writes run off-thread.

The fluent success/error overloads of capture(...), captureMap(...) and toMapItem(...), plus stream frame/error and progress consumers, dispatch on the server thread. Progress is coalesced to at most one callback per tick. Keep every callback short. Exceptions thrown by consumers fail pending work or an active stream. A final coalesced progress notification may arrive after successful completion; an exception in that notification cannot revoke the completed result.

Ordinary CompletableFuture continuations have no Bukkit thread guarantee. A continuation registered after completion can run immediately on the attaching thread; cancellation and failure may occur on a worker. Use the callback overloads for Bukkit changes, or an explicit main-thread executor. Never use join() or get() on the server thread.

The facade owns one bounded conversion worker and a queue of 32 tasks. Saturation reports QUEUE_FULL; do not create an unlimited retry queue. Large pure image() conversions run on the caller thread, so use an appropriate bounded executor. An already completed frame's pure image conversion remains usable after facade close.

Cancellation propagates to the active capture, render, conversion and saving stage. Owner disable, provider replacement and affected world unload settle pending work and suppress late consumers. Streams never queue catch-up frames or publish stale frames over a newer output. A map already allocated or a file already atomically replaced cannot be revoked by cancellation.

Low-level clients retain their existing threading contract. When bypassing the facade, explicitly own executors, tasks and lifecycle guards, and check the current provider generation before publishing output.

docs.title: Troubleshooting and support diagnostics
docs.text:
For the new fluent API, first verify the preview.3 SDK and ShutterBug Renderer 1.1.0 platform JAR with its embedded native library. NoSuchMethodError, missing autocomplete classes or UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY often mean the compile and runtime versions differ. Use setup to refresh IDE sources and compatibility to choose the correct pair. Photo-saving and map-binding recovery are described in operator storage guidance.

The commercial installation checks below apply to Renderer 1.1.0. SDK publication does not establish personalized buyer activation.

Start at the first failing boundary:

  1. Confirm Java 25, Paper 26.2, Minecraft 26.2, and a supported platform. Java 21 is the SDK compilation baseline, not this server's runtime requirement. Supported platform archives are macOS ARM64, Linux x86-64 and Windows x86-64.
  2. Verify ShutterBugRenderer.jar came from your personalized MCModels Renderer 1.1.0 download for this platform. Personalization changes the JAR and may change its enclosing ZIP, so a published checksum for the vendor's unpersonalized archive or native payload is not a byte-for-byte checksum for your download. If provenance is uncertain, retain the original purchase download, calculate its SHA-256 locally, and ask MCModels product support to check it through a private ticket; do not post the JAR or purchase identifiers publicly. The native is embedded and checksum-verified by the provider before extraction; do not copy, rename, or install a separate native file. A generic or incomplete JAR is not an activation substitute.
  3. Read the provider startup result. license-key stays blank only for a separately verified and enabled personalized-download activation flow; that production buyer gate is currently pending. An explicitly configured support-supplied manual value takes precedence for fresh activation. A valid signed cache may cover a restart only until its six-hour lease expires. The purchase permits three active hardware installations. For activation, lease, seat, trust, hardware-change, or product-mismatch errors, stop retries and follow the supported operator/admin process in operator activation.
  4. Confirm RendererService appears. Optional consumers should remain usable and attach when the service registers; hard dependencies should fail clearly.
  5. Inspect rendererVersion, platform, nativeAvailable, packagedForProduction, supported profiles, and supported attachments. Do not dump object internals or environment variables.
  6. Reproduce with the sample plugin, one small Classic render, no optional attachments, and no custom assets. Add one feature at a time.
  7. Use the typed failure recovery table. After reload, discard old clients, scenes, asset handles, and tasks.

A support bundle may contain UTC timestamp, product and SDK versions, Paper/Minecraft versions, platform key, sanitized provider startup code, capability snapshot, failure code, task phase/status, artifact SHA-256 values, and the smallest reproduction. Remove player data, world paths, network addresses, environment dumps, license values, bearer tokens, purchase identifiers, and private plugin source. Preserve the original logs locally.

docs.title: Moving to Renderer 1.1.0 and the fluent API
docs.text:
Pair the immutable 2.3.0-preview.3 SDK with ShutterBug Renderer 1.1.0 and the native library embedded in its platform JAR. Published SDK, sources and JavaDoc archives are unchanged. Update your provided/compile-only dependency and reload your IDE. A new SDK does not add support to an older provider. Existing constructors and the v1 binary baseline remain; you can migrate individual workflows to the facade without giving up manual scenes or attachments.

Start with one plugin-owned Renderer; replace ordinary photo pipelines with snapshot(...).captureMap(...) and monitors with stream(...).start(). Keep your permissions, cooldowns, recipient delivery and gameplay policies. captureMap() now saves provider-owned photo data, while raw captures and streams allocate no durable photos. Back up provider photo storage, world map data/counter and inventories together before changing deployments.

If adapting earlier development recipes, entity layers now respect scene occlusion by default. Add Occlusion.SELECTED_ONLY only where through-wall visibility is intentional. Keep exposure, final-layer brightness and FOV separate; check light limits before offering a rig to users.

docs.title: Commercial provider upgrades
docs.text:
Read release notes, confirm compatibility, and back up plugins/ShutterBugRenderer/config.yml before changing files. Drain or cancel tasks and stop the server. Replace only ShutterBugRenderer.jar with the personalized JAR from your download for that platform; its native is embedded, verified, and extracted automatically. Leave license-key blank only for a separately verified and enabled automatic MCModels buyer flow; otherwise preserve a protected support-supplied manual override. See the current activation gate. Start and verify product identity, activation, capabilities, and one disposable render.

The published free SDK v1.0.2 adds an immutable excludedEntityIds set to CaptureRequest, with a five-argument constructor and accessor. The original four-argument constructor still includes all otherwise renderable entities, and the existing v1 binary baseline is preserved. Constructor-based consumers need no source migration, but record patterns and record-component reflection must account for the fifth component when recompiling. New exclusion-aware consumers require the matching provider API. Do not shade the SDK or replace API classes inside a provider. Fresh Maven and Gradle consumers verified this release. Keep both v1.0.1 and v1.0.2 immutable; later documentation updates must not move or rewrite either tag.

For rollback, stop the server and restore the previous verified ShutterBugRenderer.jar plus its matching configuration. Do not copy or manage an extracted native cache as a release input. Recapture scenes and register assets again after either upgrade or rollback because clients, scenes, handles, and tasks belong to one provider generation.

docs.title: A small X-ray camera
docs.text: This example uses the fluent 2.3.0-preview.3 SDK and ShutterBug Renderer 1.1.0 with its matching embedded native library. The renderer supplies general selection, layering and colour controls; the addon supplies the X-ray recipe and its permission.

docs.title: The rendering request
docs.text:
package docs.examples;

import ke.ric.renderer.api.*;
import org.bukkit.entity.Player;

/** One capture, two ordered passes; captureMap() also saves the resulting photo. */
public final class XrayPipelineExample {
    public static SnapshotBuilder photo(Renderer renderer, Player viewer) {
        return renderer.snapshot(viewer).visibleTo(viewer).recipe(RenderRecipe.layers(
                RenderLayer.scene().brightness(0.2),
                RenderLayer.entities(EntitySelector.living()).occlusion(Occlusion.SELECTED_ONLY)));
    }
}

The first pass draws the scene at 20% brightness. The second draws living entities over it, explicitly using Occlusion.SELECTED_ONLY to see through unselected geometry. Both derive from one captured scene. Selected entities still obscure each other, and the scene remains available to shadow/light rays. Removing SELECTED_ONLY restores the default visible-only behaviour.

visibleTo(viewer) applies that viewer's Bukkit visibility rules. The camera entity is excluded automatically, and request exclusions/privacy cannot be undone by an X-ray pass. The final image is opaque; object-ID coverage is not a physically accurate transparency matte.

docs.title: Complete plugin
docs.text:
The complete source is one Java class plus its POM and plugin.yml. It calls captureMap(...), so conversion and durable provider storage finish before delivery. It no longer owns capture futures, pixel loops, quantization or retained map renderers.

Build with Java 21 using mvn -f examples/xray-camera/pom.xml package in the public source checkout. The resulting target/XrayCamera.jar needs the matching ShutterBugRenderer 1.1.0 on its documented Paper adapter. The local renderer source tree stores this same example under renderer-docs/examples/xray-camera/.

Run /xrayphoto as a player with xraycamera.use (operator by default). A busy flag limits this small demonstration to one photograph at a time. Its main-thread callback checks online state and drops inventory overflow at the recipient's location. A production plugin should add its own offline delivery/mailbox and permissions/cooldown policy. Saved pixels remain in provider storage if the addon disables; pending callbacks are suppressed after owner shutdown.

This is an example of general render composition, not a special X-ray rendering path. Creative controls shows ordinary photography, visible-only tinting and a camera-relative studio light using the same primitives. Do not use through-wall output on servers where it is not authorized.
